question: Which birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi was celebrated on 2ⁿd October 2023?
solution:
The Correct answer is 154th .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 154th **birth anniversary** of **Mahatma Gandhi** was celebrated on **2nd October 2023**.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi**, is one of the most celebrated leaders in **Indian history** and is regarded as the **Father of the Nation** in India.
 
• He was born on **2nd October 1869** in **Porbandar, Gujarat.**
 
• Gandhi is globally known for his philosophy of **non-violence (Ahimsa)** and his role in India's **freedom struggle** against British rule.
 
• This day is commemorated worldwide as the **International Day of Non-Violence**, as declared by the **United Nations General Assembly** in 2007.
 
• On this occasion, tributes are paid to Mahatma Gandhi at his **samadhi at Raj Ghat** in New Delhi, where prayers, cultural events, and exhibitions are organized.
 
• The day is marked by activities such as **cleanliness drives** under the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, which was inspired by Gandhi's vision of a clean and self-reliant India.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's principles of **Satyagraha (truth force)** and civil disobedience have influenced many leaders and movements worldwide, including Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi's Contributions:**__

 __
 
• He led various movements such as the **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)**, the **Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)**, and the **Quit India Movement (1942)**.
 
• He pioneered the philosophy of **self-reliance (Swadeshi)**, encouraging Indians to boycott British goods and promote local industries.
 
• He emphasized the importance of **communal harmony** and worked tirelessly to bridge gaps between various communities in India.
 
• His autobiography, **"The Story of My Experiments with Truth,"** is widely read and provides deep insights into his personal journey and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 2nd October:**__
 
 
• The day is observed as a national holiday in India to honor Mahatma Gandhi's contributions to the nation.
 
• It is also celebrated as **Lal Bahadur Shastri Jayanti**, as **Lal Bahadur Shastri**, India's second Prime Minister, was born on the same day in **1904**.
 
• Globally, the day is recognized as a symbol of peace and non-violence.
